body: Morning thesis is being tested harder than the base case: the negative open happened, pero mas important, the prior TOPIX/breadth cushion also broke—Reuters says more than 90% of Prime names were down by lunch. That upgrades the signal from yesterday's rotation story to broad de-risking. The transmission chain remains oil + global yields + Japan rates; if breadth stays this weak into the close, the evening scorecard should treat the opening call as correct but the breadth deterioration as materially worse than hoped.

claims.text: At the September 2 midday break, the Nikkei 225 was down 2.63% at 64,473.16 and more than 90% of TSE Prime stocks were lower.
The morning move represents broader de-risking than the September 1 rotation because weakness has spread across most Prime Market stocks.
claims.basis: Inference from broad decliner share versus the prior article's positive breadth baseline.

body: From a market lens, huwag i-equate ang reward cut automatically with a clean earnings win for Docomo. The same design is steering spending toward d-payments and smartphone tap while giving some fee-card users an exit/refund route. So the real economic question is net: lower reward cost versus retention, payment volume, card mix and ecosystem engagement. For households, the article's advice is stronger than any corporate inference—calculate your own net value first.

claims.text: The announced reward redesign does not by itself establish a positive or negative net earnings impact for Docomo because customer retention, payment mix and ecosystem behavior can offset changes in reward expense.
claims.basis: Market-economics inference from the article's documented reward cuts, retained higher-return payment paths and refund option; no earnings impact is asserted as fact.
